concepts.def: Jobs: der Arzt/die Ärztin (doctor), der Lehrer/die Lehrerin (teacher), der Ingenieur (engineer), der Anwalt (lawyer).
Most German jobs have masculine + feminine forms: Lehrer / Lehrerin, Arzt / Ärztin, Student / Studentin (-in suffix).
'Ich möchte...werden' (I would like to become...), 'Ich werde...studieren' (I will study...).
German training: die Ausbildung (apprenticeship), das Praktikum (work placement), die Lehre (apprenticeship).
Workplace: der Arbeitsplatz, der Chef (boss), das Gehalt (salary), das Vorstellungsgespräch (job interview).
Adjective endings depend on case + article: 'ein guter Job' (nom), 'einen guten Job' (acc), 'einem guten Job' (dat).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area D: The World of Work — a core area of GCSE German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area D: The World of Work brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area D: The World of Work.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence means 'I want to become a doctor' (female speaker)?
options: Ich möchte Ärztin werden.
Ich möchte ein Arzt werden.
Ich möchte Arzt werden bin.
Ich werde möchte Arzt sein.
a work placement
a salary
a boss
a CV

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'ich will' and 'ich möchte'?
options: Ich will is future tense.
They mean the same thing.
Macht!
Ich will = I want (strong, direct); ich möchte = I would like (polite).

mcqs.q: What is the imperative 'du' form of 'machen' (to do)?
options: Du machst!
Macht!
Mach! (drop -en, sometimes drop -st).
Ich will is future tense.

mcqs.q: Where does 'nicht' go in 'I don't like the film' (Der Film gefällt mir nicht)?
options: At the end (negating the whole sentence).
Macht!
Before the verb.
Right after the subject.
